claim: The Rulers row's description reads 'Horizontal and vertical rulers along canvas edges. Click+drag from ruler to place a manual guide line.'
truth: No user can place a guide. Two independent reasons. (1) There is no drag gesture — RulersOverlay exposes onClick only, never mousedown/mousemove-drag (RulersOverlay.tsx:119 and :214). (2) The click cannot land: the overlay root sets pointerEvents:'none' (CanvasOverlayGroup.tsx:206) and RulersOverlay never re-enables it — `grep -n "pointerEvents" src/editor/canvas/overlays/RulersOverlay.tsx` returns nothing, while its sibling GuidesOverlay does re-enable it per guide (GuidesOverlay.tsx:161). So the ruler canvases carry cursor:'pointer' and an onClick that no pointer event ever reaches, and onMouseMove never fires either (the hover indicator never paints). The persistence layer behind it is complete and correct and has no reachable caller: useCanvasGuides.ts:84-94 addGuide, :15 STORAGE_KEY 'buildrick-guides', :38-59 load/save. Rulers also sit INSIDE the canvas content box at top:0/left:0 (RulersOverlay.tsx:111-113, :205-208), overlaying the customer's page rather than sitting along the frame edge as the board draws them.
evidence: RulersOverlay.tsx:119, :214 (onClick, no drag handler); CanvasOverlayGroup.tsx:206 (pointerEvents:'none' on the overlay root); GuidesOverlay.tsx:161 (pointerEvents:'auto' — the contrast that proves the omission); useCanvasGuides.ts:84-94, :15, :38-59; RulersOverlay.tsx:111-113, :205-208 (positioning). target: 25 · Reference / 96:6  Device frames + zoom — §5.5  (Zoom rules block)
claim: The 'Zoom rules' block states: zoom-to-fit runs as (canvas − 48) / frameWidth clamped 25–100%; manual range 25–200%; steps 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 / 200.
truth: Every one of those four numbers disagrees with the shipped code, AND with board 817:4723 in the same file — two boards describing one control contradict each other, so at least one is wrong regardless of the code. The code sides with 817:4723. (a) Zoom-to-fit subtracts 64px, not 48, and takes the minimum of BOTH axes, not width alone: Canvas.tsx:309-324. (b) Its clamp is Math.max(0.1, Math.min(5, scale)) = 10–500%, not 25–100% — Canvas.tsx:322-323. (c) The manual preset list is [10,25,50,75,100,150,200,400], so the range is 10–400 and there is no 125% step at all. (d) Zoom-to-selection, which this block omits entirely, clamps at Math.min(4, scale) = 400% and additionally scrollIntoView-centres the element (Canvas.tsx:331-348).
evidence: Canvas.tsx:309-324 (handleFitToScreen: client box minus 64px padding, scale = Math.min(vw/cw, vh/ch), clamped 0.1–5, then composer.setZoom(Math.round(clamped*100))); Canvas.tsx:331-348 (handleZoomToSelection, Math.min(4, scale) + scrollIntoView({block:'center',inline:'center'})); shared/constants/canvas.ts:360 (ZOOM_PRESETS, no 125); shared/constants/config.ts:87-90 (THRESHOLDS ZOOM_MIN 10 / ZOOM_MAX 500 — the engine clamp Composer.setZoom uses at Composer.ts:1044, which is why fit can legitimately return 500%, a value the preset list cannot represent). Board interiors of both 96:6 and 817:4723 read with an explicit stack walk.

Saving works end to end: it exports the page, runs inverseResolveTokens so the HTML carries {{token.*}} placeholders rather than this site's hexes, writes to localStorage MY_TEMPLATES, mirrors to the server through a retry queue, and raises a coalesced 'Template saved on this device only' notice on failure. target: 1084:4527 / 642:2832 · 1169:4713  (what applying actually does, and its undo)
claim: The applying and replace-confirm boards imply that applying a template replaces the page, and the file has no board asserting it lands as one undo step.
truth: Both are correct and now measured. APPLY ALWAYS REPLACES — never appends, never inserts: importHTMLToActivePage deletes every descendant of the page root from the element map and then assigns `page.root.children = children`. There is no append mode reachable from the Templates panel; the TemplateLoadOptions.mergeStrategy type in shared/types has no consumer, and the TemplateManager that would have used it is marked @deprecated DEAD/SIMULATED at its first line. ONE UNDO STEP — yes, for the import: it runs inside a named transaction which defers the single PROJECT_CHANGED emit to endTransaction, and HistoryManager records once per burst with a 500ms coalesce window. Two side effects sit OUTSIDE that transaction and can therefore land as separate history entries: createPage + setActivePage in new-page mode, and styles.clear() when 'Reset global styles' is ticked. One consequence worth a caption: the history entry is labelled from the transaction, so a user who applied 'SaaS Landing' sees 'Imported HTML' in the History panel, not the template's name.

claim: W-F-29 records that the board promises 'Your brand tokens are applied automatically' while the shipped copy says the opposite, and proposes conforming the board to the code.
truth: Agree with the direction, with one measured correction that matters for a destructive-action dialog. W-F-29's evidence says templatesData.ts contains no reference to a design token. Literally true of `var()` — but there are FOUR {{token.color.primary}} placeholders across THREE of the ten templates (SaaS Landing ×2, Startup ×1, Coming Soon ×1), and they DO resolve: the apply path snapshots the live design system off :root and substitutes them before sanitizing and importing, leaving misses verbatim. So for three templates the primary CTA colour IS re-mapped to the site's brand; the other seven hardcode their palette. The shipped sentence 'your brand tokens are not applied to it' therefore overstates slightly in the safe direction, which is the right way to be wrong on a dialog that destroys work. The second checkbox W-F-29 wants drawn is 'Reset global styles to template defaults', and its sibling 'Save the current page as a backup version first' defaults to ON — the code comment explains why (on an action that destroys work the safe option is the default).
evidence: `grep -o "{{token\.[a-z.]*}}" src/editor/sidebar/tabs/templates/templatesData.ts | sort | uniq -c` → 4 × {{token.color.primary}}, in the templates at ids site-saas-landing, site-startup and site-coming-soon. Resolver: utils/resolveTemplateTokens.ts:19 (PLACEHOLDER_RE), :47-59 (substitute, miss returns the placeholder verbatim), :61-63 (DOMPurify with ADD_ATTR data-buildrick-id). Called at TemplatesTab.tsx:253-254 (`const snapshot = snapshotFromComputedStyle(document.documentElement, DEFAULT_TOKENS); const resolvedHtml = resolveTokens(t.html, snapshot);`). Shipped copy and both checkboxes: TemplatesTabModals.tsx:109-116, :117-122 (backup, default ON per TemplatesTab.tsx:114), :124-130 (reset global styles).
edit: Adopt W-F-29's fix. When rewriting the sentence, use the shipped wording verbatim ('The template brings its own colours and type — your brand tokens are not applied to it.') rather than inventing a hedge, and draw BOTH checkboxes with 'Save the current page as a backup version first' checked by default.

claim: 781:4372 draws a load-error panel; 778:4102 'Templates · loading' was RETIRED 2026-09-02 as having no producer.
truth: The load-error board has a real producer and correct copy: a server hydrate of the user's saved templates can fail, and the drawer renders 'Couldn't load templates.' / 'You can keep building from Insert.' / 'Try again', with the retry re-running the hydrate. Board is right. The retirement of 778:4102 is also right — but its stated reason is not, and I am recording that without re-opening it. A producer DOES exist: the hydrate sets state 'loading' before fetching. What is missing is a CONSUMER — the drawer renders only the 'error' branch, so nothing ever draws a loading state. Retiring the board was correct; the note should say 'no consumer', not 'no producer', so the next audit does not go looking for the emitter and find one.
evidence: Producer: services/templateSync.ts:43 (`export type TemplateHydrateState = "idle" | "loading" | "error" | "ready";`), :133 setHydrateState('loading'), :153 ('ready'), :155 ('error'), :128 hydrateUserTemplatesFromServer. target: 1084:4527 / section-level — the two template type systems
claim: Boards in this section carry facts like ratings, downloads, price, author and 'updated <date>'.
truth: Two Template types exist and only one ships. The marketplace type — Template extends TemplateMetadata with category, tags, author, thumbnail, previews, version, createdAt, updatedAt, premium, price, downloads, rating, license — is consumed only by the deprecated TemplateManager and TemplateEngine; all eight TEMPLATE_* events it emits have zero listeners, and engine:templates is one of the six fully isolated modules in EVENT-GRAPH.json. The shipping type is TemplateItem, whose entire field set is id, name, type, icon, html, description, status, category, industry, gradient, pageCount, subCategory, version. So any board fact outside that list has no field behind it — which is the root cause of W-F-34's 'updated 12 Jun'. Also note PAGE_TEMPLATE_ATTACHED, PAGE_TEMPLATE_DETACHED and TAB_NAVIGATE_TEMPLATE are declared and never named anywhere; the applied-template link is persisted on Page.meta.appliedTemplates instead and read by useTemplateUsageMap, which is why the usage drawer works without the event bus.

Shipping type: editor/sidebar/tabs/templates/templatesData.ts:27-50. Event evidence from findings/EVENT-GRAPH.json: TEMPLATE_LOADED / SAVED / LOADING / ERROR / DELETED / SOURCE_REGISTERED / CACHE_CLEARED and TEMPLATES_IMPORTED all in the emitted-with-no-listener set; PAGE_TEMPLATE_ATTACHED, PAGE_TEMPLATE_DETACHED, TAB_NAVIGATE_TEMPLATE in the declared-but-never-named set; isolated modules list includes engine:templates. Live path: TemplatesTab.tsx:311-317 recordAppliedTemplate; hooks/useTemplateUsageMap.ts.
